item: Land two more researched setback updates: Georgetown (rewrite-reflecting SF districts) and San Marcos (relabel + a gating live GIS check).
checkpoint: DONE. legacy-design-tools PR #631 merged to main (9bf4aca6), branch deleted.

georgetown.whatShipped: MERGE, not replace, into the existing georgetown-tx.json. The 3 pre-rewrite single-family districts (RE Residential Estate, RL Residential Low Density, RS Residential Single-Family) are replaced with 4 districts from the City's adopted-but-not-yet-effective UDC rewrite (Council adopted 2026-08-11; effective 2026-11-01 per the rewrite's own Section 1.09): RE Residential Estate District, RT Residential Traditional District, RS Residential Suburban District, RM Residential Mix District. The 9 non-single-family districts (TF, TH, MF-1, MF-2, CN, C-1, C-3, OF, IN) are preserved completely unchanged -- still accurate under the currently-governing code, and there is no research to replace them with. A clean full-table replacement would have silently dropped real, still-accurate coverage in exchange for narrower new coverage; caught and flagged before doing that, operator/peer explicitly ruled merge over replace.
georgetown.verificationStateDecision: The 4 new districts are primary-source-verified, not human-verified, despite Georgetown having a real 658-atom code-section corpus (unlike the four zero-corpus cities landed earlier tonight). Confirmed live before deciding: zero real atoms mention the rewrite's district name 'Residential Traditional'; several mention the pre-rewrite name 'Residential Low Density'. The real corpus only contains currently-in-force text -- there is nothing to round-trip rewrite quotes against regardless of the corpus's size. This is a distinct finding from the earlier Killeen/Round Rock pattern (real corpus, real round-trip achievable) and from Belton/Seguin/Cibolo (no corpus at all).
georgetown.knownPreExistingIssueLeftAlone: The 9 preserved districts carry the same fabricated 'georgetown_tx/udc/<section>' atom_did convention found and fixed everywhere else tonight, predating this session's work entirely. Left alone per explicit instruction to keep them as-is (they are out of scope for tonight's rewrite-driven update); documented in a test assertion rather than silently carried forward or silently fixed without discussion.
georgetown.followUpFlagged: Once the rewrite is closer to taking effect or after 2026-11-01, the other 9 districts will need the same post-rewrite research the 4 SF districts just got, or the table permanently carries two vintages at once. Not blocking, not done here.

sanMarcos.whatShipped: Relabel only -- same 8 districts (SF-6, SF-4.5, and 6 legacy-named non-SF districts MU/CC/GC/P/NC/OP) and identical numeric values to what was already registered, confirmed field-by-field before touching anything. Fixes the same fabricated-atom_did / mislabeled-human-verified pattern found in every zero-corpus city tonight (san_marcos_tx has zero real code-section atoms, live-confirmed).
sanMarcos.gatingLiveCheck: Landing was gated on a real, live GIS check before touching the file, per explicit instruction: queried the real zoning layer (smgis.sanmarcostx.gov) with an area-weighted group-by on ZONECODE (not raw polygon count, which would be misleading -- one large polygon vs many small ones). The two covered current-code districts (SF-6 + SF-4.5) account for 12.93% of the city's total zoned area; the legacy Chapter 9 system they supersede (D + DR + TH) accounts for 0.90%, and SF-11 no longer appears in the live layer at all (every parcel once so zoned has already been rezoned). Roughly 14:1 dominance, clearing the bar to land. Correction to an earlier verbal report: SF-R (2.46% of area) is a separate current-code district this research explicitly does not cover, not part of either the covered or legacy figures -- the precise comparison is 12.93% vs 0.90%, not the looser 15.39%-vs-0.90% first reported before double-checking the file's own OMITTED list.

testing: New georgetownRewriteSanMarcosSetbacks.test.ts (8 tests) plus an update to the pre-existing f4lSetbackTables.test.ts's Georgetown spot-check (intentional data change, not a regression -- old district names/values no longer exist). Full lib/adapters suite: 413 passing. lib/cad-ingest unaffected: 288 passing. tsc --build clean. CI green (Test job 12m0s).
